title: Coalescence Controller: workload profiling, adaptive coalescing heuristics, and safe rollout
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a production-safe Coalescence Controller that produces per-route coalescing (batching) recommendations derived from continuous workload profiling and applies configuration changes with automated safety gates and rollback.

Background: We see material token-cost savings when requests are coalesced intelligently, but naive config flips cause tail latency regressions for latency-sensitive routes. This ticket scopes a runtime-side controller plus a safe apply/rollback flow that can be used by both Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Design summary:
1) Workload profiling: lightweight, continuous sampler that exposes per-route arrival process (inter-arrival histogram), token-length distribution, prefix cache-hit rate, and p95/p99 latency conditioned on small/large sequences. Profiles are stored as compressed fingerprints for quick diffing.
2) Heuristic engine: set of interpretable rules that propose coalescing parameter deltas (hold_window_us, min_coalesce_tokens, max_coalesce_ms, max_batch_size). Rules consider route SLO tier, inferred arrival burstiness, and cache-effect to avoid increasing KV cache churn.
3) Continuous parameters: parameters evolve via an annealing controller — start conservative (short hold window, low max batch size) and expand when utilization and tail latency headroom permit. Parameters include decay_rate, exploration_delta, and safety_margin_pct.
4) Safe apply and rollback: canary rollout by route percentage, metric-based verification (p50/p95 latency, error rate, tail-QPS), automated rollback if thresholds cross. Adds idempotent config apply API with dry-run and simulated-traffic mode.

Why this is novel: Prior work has focused on static batch profiles or offline autotuning. This controller is online, workload-aware, explicitly cache-aware, and built with explicit rollback and circuit-breaker behavior so we can ship per-route gains without manual toil.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller runs in staging and produces profile fingerprints for 90% of instrumented routes.
2) Heuristic proposals are emitted and surfaced as a diff via the Console UI mock endpoint.
3) Canary apply path: rollouts to 5%/25%/100% increments with automated metric checks (p95 latency +3% threshold, error rate +0.2% absolute).
4) Automated rollback triggers within 10 minutes of threshold breach and restores previous config cleanly.
5) End-to-end e2e test covering dry-run, simulated-traffic validation, and rollback path.
6) Documentation + runbook describing expected signals and manual override steps.
steps:
1) Instrument lightweight per-request telemetry and build continuous sampler (Ravi).
2) Prototype profile fingerprint format (gzip+protobuf) and fingerprint comparator (Luis).
3) Implement heuristic engine with declarative rule set and unit tests (Maya).
4) Add idempotent config apply API + dry-run + simulated mode (backend team).
5) Integrate canary rollout orchestration and metric checks (SLO infra).
6) Build dashboard surface in Console mock and add approval flow (PM + DX).
7) Run internal dogfood on non-critical routes for 4 weeks and iterate thresholds.
8) Prepare runbook and safety postmortem template for rollout to customers.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Ravi Kapoor: Kickoff notes — scoped minimal viable heuristic set: hold_window_us, max_batch_size, min_coalesce_tokens, and exploration_delta. Decided to make profiler sampling non-blocking with bounded memory (circular buffers).

2026-02-25 - Maya Chen: POC done for sampler; we can compute arrival CV and a 5-bin inter-arrival histogram in <1% CPU for our high-throughput frontend. Uploaded profiler sketch to drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/profiles/ENG-725001/proto-sketch

2026-03-01 - Luis Ortega: Fingerprint comparator implemented; uses Jensen-Shannon on token-length + arrival histogram and a heuristic score combining p95 headroom. Added unit tests and a small simulation harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345

2026-03-05 - Jasmine Park (PM): Updated canary policy to require both latency and KV cache hit stability checks. See design note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Coalescence+Controller+Design
2026-03-09 - SLO Infra (note): Metric checks prototype wired to alert engine; configured threshold defaults: p95 +3%, error_rate +0.2% absolute, kv_cache_hit_drop >2% triggers rollback.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Started implementing rollout orchestration — canary increments, timers, and circuit breaker. Found race when two controllers attempt concurrent applies; added optimistic locking via config-version header.
notes:
Risk: incorrectly increasing hold_window_us on latency-sensitive routes may cause customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults, explicit SLO classification, and automatic rollback.
Next milestone (by 2026-03-20): first internal canary run on 10 low-SLO routes.
final_comment: Ready for review by runtime team. Working on end-to-end tests and runbook. Will schedule a demo for Platform Sync next week.
